definitions.gloss: incense; fragrant substance burned for its scent
definitions.explanation: Aromatic materials, typically in stick or cone form, burned to produce pleasant fragrance. Used in religious ceremonies, meditation, and as home fragrance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{寝|ね}る→寝る：00470_neru⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{香|こう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焚|た}く→焚く：02285_taku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{眠|ねむ}れる→眠れる：15166_nemureru⟧。
examples.english: Burning incense before bed helps me sleep well.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{香|こう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焚|た}いている→焚く：02285_taku⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother burns incense in front of the Buddhist altar every morning.

notes:
The polite prefix お is standard for this word; plain ⟦{香|こう}→香：17307_kou⟧ is used in compounds but rarely alone in everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{香|こう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焚|た}く→焚く：02285_taku⟧: to burn incense
- お{香|こう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{供|そな}える→供える：11562_sonaeru⟧: to offer incense
- お{香|こう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧: the scent of incense
- ⟦{線香|せんこう}→線香：09995_senkou⟧: stick incense

CULTURAL NOTE:
Incense has deep roots in Japanese culture, used in Buddhist ceremonies, tea ceremony, and the traditional art of ⟦{香道|こうどう}→香道：29522_koudou⟧ (the Way of Incense). Modern use includes aromatherapy and home fragrance. Common types include {白檀|びゃくだん} (sandalwood) and {沈香|じんこう} (agarwood).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{線香|せんこう}→線香：09995_senkou⟧: stick incense — specifically the thin sticks used at altars and graves
- ⟦{香料|こうりょう}→香料：14678_kouryou⟧: fragrance materials — broader term including perfumery ingredients
- アロマ: aroma — modern loanword for aromatherapy-style fragrance
